entities.summary:
Ludwig von Erlichshausen (1410–1467) was the 31st Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, serving from 1449/1450 to 1467.

As Grand Master, he played a crucial role in the Teutonic Knights' expansion and consolidation of their territories in Prussia and Livonia, particularly during the Livonian War.

His leadership during this period saw the Knights achieve significant victories against the Lithuanians and Russians, securing key victories at the Battle of Saule and the Battle of Grunwald.

Despite his military successes, von Erlichshausen's tenure was also marked by controversy and internal strife within the Order, as he struggled to maintain the Knights' influence and power in a rapidly changing European landscape.

The legacy of von Erlichshausen's leadership can be seen in the continued presence of the Teutonic Knights in Prussia and the Baltic region, and his influence on the development of the Order's military tactics and strategies.

In the years following his death, von Erlichshausen's reputation as a skilled military leader and statesman was cemented by his successors, who continued to draw on his example and build on his achievements.

The inscription on his tombstone at the Marienkirche in Königsberg, which reads 'Ludwig von Erlichshausen, 31st Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights', serves as a poignant reminder of his enduring legacy in the annals of European history.

The impact of von Erlichshausen's leadership can also be seen in the contemporary accounts of the time, such as those of the Polish historian and chronicler, Jan Długosz, who wrote extensively on the Teutonic Knights' military campaigns and von Erlichshausen's role in them.

Despite the passing of centuries, von Erlichshausen's name remains synonymous with the Teutonic Knights and their military prowess, a testament to his enduring influence on the course of European history.
